pages.title: What this unit is about
pages.body:
> 💻 **Strand 1 — Introduction To Computing**
Sub-strand 2: Technology in the Community

Technology should serve everyone, including people with disabilities. In this unit you will learn about assistive technologies, examine how portable devices affect our lives, and evaluate the issues that come with online services.

pages.title: Content standard and lessons
pages.body:
> 🎯 **Content standard**
- **B8.1.2.1** Demonstrate the use of technology in the community.

> 🧭 **What you will be able to do**
- **B8.1.2.1.1** Discuss technologies that help to improve computer accessibility (adaptive and assistive technologies).
- **B8.1.2.1.2** Describe how portable computing devices affect our everyday lives.
- **B8.1.2.1.3** Explain the issues associated with online services (social media, wikis, blogs, etc.).

> 🗺️ **Lessons in this unit**
- 2.1 Adaptive and Assistive Technologies
- 2.2 Portable Computing Devices in Everyday Life
- 2.3 Issues Associated with Online Services

**Core competencies developed:** Digital Literacy (DL5.3), Communication and Collaboration (CC8.1).

pages.title: Adaptive and Assistive Technologies
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B8.1.2.1.1
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- identify categories of people with special needs;
- discuss technologies that help people with special needs use computers and mobile devices.
**Accessibility** means designing technology so that everyone, including persons with disabilities, can use it. **Assistive technology** is any device or software that helps a person with a disability to do something they would otherwise find difficult. **Adaptive technology** modifies standard equipment for a particular need (e.g. a keyboard with large keys).

pages.title: Adaptive and Assistive Technologies (continued)
pages.body:
| **Category of special need** | **Assistive / adaptive technologies** |
|---|---|
| Visual impairment (blind or low vision) | **Screen readers** that read text aloud (Windows **Narrator**, free **NVDA**, JAWS, TalkBack on Android, VoiceOver on iPhone); **screen magnifiers** (Windows Magnifier); **contrast themes**; refreshable **Braille displays**; Braille embossers; large-print keyboards |
| Hearing impairment (deaf or hard of hearing) | **Live captions** and subtitles; speech-to-text apps; visual alerts (flashing notifications); video calls for sign language; hearing aids that connect by Bluetooth |
| Physical / mobility impairment | **Voice recognition** (Windows **Voice Access**, voice typing); **on-screen keyboard**; **Sticky Keys** (press shortcut keys one at a time); trackballs, joysticks and large-key keyboards; head pointers, eye-tracking (**Eye Control**), sip-and-puff switches |
| Speech impairment | Text-to-speech apps; communication boards and AAC (augmentative and alternative communication) devices |
| Learning difficulties (e.g. dyslexia) | **Immersive Reader** (reads text aloud and highlights words), spelling and grammar tools, dyslexia-friendly fonts, mind-mapping software |
| **Windows 11 accessibility shortcut** | **Action** |
|---|---|
| Windows + Ctrl + Enter | Turn Narrator on/off |
| Windows + Plus (+) | Open Magnifier |
| Windows + H | Voice typing |
| Windows + Ctrl + L | Live captions |
| Windows + Ctrl + O | On-screen keyboard |
| Press Shift five times | Sticky Keys |

pages.title: Adaptive and Assistive Technologies (continued)
pages.body:
> 💻 **Practical session**
Open **Settings › Accessibility**. In pairs, turn on **Narrator** and listen to it read a web page; use **Magnifier** to zoom into text; try **Voice typing** (Windows + H) to dictate a sentence into Word. Discuss how each tool helps a person with special needs.
> 🇬🇭 **Ghana connection** Ghana’s **Persons with Disability Act, 2006 (Act 715)** supports equal access for persons with disabilities. Inclusive education means every learner, with or without a disability, should be able to use ICT tools in school.

pages.title: Portable Computing Devices in Everyday Life
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B8.1.2.1.2
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- discuss portable computing devices used daily;
- describe how these devices affect our daily lives.
| **Device** | **Everyday uses** |
|---|---|
| Smartphone | Calls, messaging, Mobile Money, photos, navigation, learning apps, news, entertainment |
| Tablet | E-books, video lessons, drawing, games, video calls |
| Laptop / Chromebook | Schoolwork, office work, programming, online classes |
| Smartwatch / fitness band | Time, notifications, step counting, heart-rate monitoring, sleep tracking |
| E-reader (e.g. Kindle) | Reading thousands of books on one device |
| Portable media player, handheld game console, digital camera | Entertainment and photography |
| **Positive effects** | **Negative effects** |
|---|---|
| Instant communication anywhere | Addiction and distraction from studies |
| Cashless payments (Mobile Money, cards) | Eye strain, poor posture (“text neck”), poor sleep |
| Access to information and online learning | Cyberbullying and exposure to harmful content |
| Navigation and transport apps (ride-hailing) | Theft of devices and data; scams |
| Health monitoring and emergency calls | Less face-to-face interaction; road accidents from using phones while walking or driving |
| New businesses and jobs | Costs of data and devices; e-waste |

pages.title: Portable Computing Devices in Everyday Life (continued)
pages.body:
> 🧪 **Activity — Digital diary**
For one day, record every time you or your family use a portable device and why. Classify each use as positive or negative, then suggest two habits to reduce the negative effects.

pages.title: Issues Associated with Online Services
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B8.1.2.1.3
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- identify online services learners use;
- evaluate issues associated with online service delivery.
**Online services** are services delivered over the Internet: social media, **wikis** (websites that many users can edit, e.g. Wikipedia), **blogs** (online journals), email, video streaming, online shopping, online banking and Mobile Money, e-government services (e.g. Ghana.gov, the GRA tax portal, passport applications) and e-learning.
| **Issue** | **Explanation** |
|---|---|
| Privacy | Services collect personal data (location, contacts, browsing). Data can be sold, leaked or misused. |
| Security and fraud | Phishing, fake online shops, account hacking and Mobile Money scams. |
| Reliability of information | Wikis and blogs can be edited by anyone; information may be wrong or biased. Check other sources. |
| Misinformation and fake news | False stories spread quickly on social media. |
| Cyberbullying and harassment | Hurtful messages, threats and humiliation online. |
| Copyright and plagiarism | Copying content without permission or acknowledgement. |
| Addiction and health | Excessive time online affects sleep, studies and relationships. |
| Digital divide and cost | Not everyone can afford devices or data; rural areas may lack connectivity. |
| Service downtime | When systems fail (e.g. Internet outages), people cannot access services. |
| Age restrictions | Many services require users to be 13+; children may meet inappropriate content. |

pages.title: Issues Associated with Online Services (continued)
pages.body:
> 🧪 **Activity — Evaluate**
In groups, choose one online service you use (e.g. WhatsApp, YouTube, Wikipedia, Mobile Money). List three benefits and three issues, rate how serious each issue is, and propose a solution for each.

pages.title: Review: written and practical tasks
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Review exercises** — answer these in your exercise book or on the computer, then check with your teacher.
## Short answer questions
1. Explain the difference between assistive and adaptive technology.
2. Name **two** technologies each for persons with visual, hearing and mobility impairments.
3. Describe **three** positive and **three** negative effects of portable devices.
4. Evaluate **four** issues associated with online services.
